name: Spider

features.claim: A spider's body is in two parts joined by a small cylindrical section.
features.quote: In spiders, the cephalothorax and abdomen are connected by a small cylindrical section, the pedicel.

features.claim: The front part of a spider's body is covered on top by a single rounded shell.
features.quote: The upper surface of the cephalothorax is covered by a single, convex carapace, while the underside is covered by two rather flat plates.

features.claim: A spider's rear body part is soft and shaped like an egg.
features.quote: The abdomen is soft and egg-shaped.
They have eight legs, and mouthparts (chelicerae) with fangs that inject venom.
Unlike insects, spiders do not have antennae.

features.claim: A spider has four pairs of eyes on the top-front of its body.
features.quote: Spiders have primarily four pairs of eyes on the top-front area of the cephalothorax, arranged in patterns that vary from one family to another.

features.claim: A spider has short, movable spinnerets at the back that give out silk.
features.quote: The abdomen has no appendages except those that have been modified to form one to four (usually three) pairs of short, movable spinnerets, which emit silk.

features.claim: A spider's whole body is covered in a shell made of chitin and proteins.
features.quote: As arthropods, they have: segmented bodies with jointed limbs, all covered in a cuticle made of chitin and proteins

features.claim: A spider's body is covered with bristles that sense touch and chemicals.
features.quote: Various touch sensors, mostly bristles called setae, respond to different levels of force, from strong contact to very weak air currents.

features.claim: Spiders that hunt without webs have dense tufts of fine bristles between the claws at the tips of their legs.
features.quote: Most spiders that hunt actively, rather than relying on webs, have dense tufts of fine bristles between the paired claws at the tips of their legs.

not_this.claim: A spider does not have antennae on its head.
not_this.quote: Unlike insects, spiders do not have antennae.

quote_not_in_the_page.claim: A spider's fangs are hollow like needles.
quote_not_in_the_page.quote: The fangs are hollow, like the needles used to give injections.

second_reading.claim: Each leg is made of seven separate parts and ends in a claw.
second_reading.quote: Each of the eight legs of a spider consists of seven distinct parts.
second_reading.why: the sentence does not support it

second_reading.claim: A spider's legs do not have muscles that push them out; they are straightened by fluid pressure.
second_reading.quote: Unlike most arthropods, spiders have no extensor muscles in their limbs and instead extend them by hydraulic pressure.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Scientists argue about whether the front body part should be called a cephalothorax.
second_reading.quote: there exists an argument against the validity of the term cephalothorax, which means fused cephalon (head) and the thorax
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Scientists argue about whether the rear body part should be called an abdomen.
second_reading.quote: arguments can be formed against the use of the term "abdomen", as the opisthosoma of all spiders contains a heart and respiratory organs, organs atypical of an abdomen
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The number of spider families recorded differs between the two sources.
second_reading.quote: As of January 2026, 53,680 spider species in 139 families have been recorded by taxonomists.
